segments.text: Here is the complete toolkit for the mole, and the heart of it is one idea, everything passes through moles.
First the atomic mass unit, one unit is one twelfth the mass of a carbon twelve atom, about one point six six times ten to the minus twenty four grams.
Now the mole triangle, moles equal mass over molar mass, equal number over Avogadro's number, equal volume over molar volume.
See it as a hub, mass, number and gas volume each connect to moles by one clean step, so route every conversion through the centre.
The molar volume V m is twenty two point four litres per mole, but only for a gas at S T P.
Average atomic mass is the sum of each isotopic mass times its abundance, divided by the total abundance, a weighted mean.
And vapour density equals molar mass over two, so molar mass is twice the vapour density, because vapour density is defined relative to hydrogen gas.
One more, the number of atoms is the number of molecules times the atomicity, and then times Avogadro's number.
ये रहा mole का पूरा toolkit, और इसका दिल एक ही idea है, सब कुछ moles से होकर गुज़रता है।
पहले atomic mass unit, one unit carbon twelve atom के mass का one twelfth है, लगभग one point six six times ten to the minus twenty four grams.
अब mole triangle, moles बराबर mass बटा molar mass, बराबर number बटा Avogadro's number, बराबर volume बटा molar volume.
इसे एक hub की तरह देखो, mass, number और gas volume हर एक moles से एक clean step में जुड़ता है, तो हर conversion को center से route करो।
Molar volume V m है twenty two point four litres per mole, पर सिर्फ़ S T P पर gas के लिए।
Average atomic mass है हर isotopic mass गुणा उसकी abundance का sum, बटा total abundance, एक weighted mean.
और vapour density बराबर molar mass बटा two, तो molar mass vapour density का दुगना है, क्योंकि vapour density hydrogen gas के relative define होती है।
एक और, atoms की संख्या है molecules की संख्या गुणा atomicity, और फिर गुणा Avogadro's number.

sections.title: Moles, atoms, and the maximum-atoms trap

board_events.text: Moles and atoms in 13.5 g of aluminium
Which has the MOST atoms?
4 g H₂ = 2 mol × 2 = 4 mol atoms; 16 g O₂ = 0.5 × 2 = 1 mol atoms.
23 g Na = 1 mol atoms; 4 g He = 1 mol atoms.
For atom-counting, always ask: monoatomic or diatomic?

segments.text: Let's make the mole hub a reflex. First, how many moles and atoms are in thirteen point five grams of aluminium, atomic mass twenty seven.
Moles is mass over molar mass, thirteen point five over twenty seven, which is zero point five moles.
Aluminium is treated as monoatomic here, so the number of atoms is zero point five times Avogadro's number, three point zero one one times ten to the twenty three atoms.
<chuckle>Now a classic speed trap, which sample has the most atoms?
Four grams of hydrogen gas is two moles of molecules, but times two for diatomic gives four moles of atoms, while sixteen grams of oxygen is half a mole times two, only one mole of atoms.
Twenty three grams of sodium is one mole of atoms, and four grams of helium is one mole of atoms, both monoatomic.
So the maximum is the four grams of hydrogen, with four moles of atoms.
The lesson, for atom counting always ask first, is this species monoatomic or diatomic, before you compare.
Mole hub को reflex बनाते हैं। पहला, thirteen point five grams aluminium में कितने moles और atoms हैं, atomic mass twenty seven.
Moles है mass बटा molar mass, thirteen point five बटा twenty seven, जो है zero point five moles.
Aluminium को यहाँ monoatomic माना जाता है, तो atoms की संख्या है zero point five गुणा Avogadro's number, three point zero one one times ten to the twenty three atoms.
<chuckle>अब एक classic speed trap, किस sample में सबसे ज़्यादा atoms हैं?
चार grams hydrogen gas दो moles molecules है, पर diatomic के लिए गुणा two से चार moles atoms, जबकि sixteen grams oxygen आधा mole गुणा two, सिर्फ़ एक mole atoms.
Twenty three grams sodium एक mole atoms है, और चार grams helium एक mole atoms, दोनों monoatomic.
तो maximum है चार grams hydrogen, चार moles atoms के साथ।
Lesson, atom counting में हमेशा पहले पूछो, ये species monoatomic है या diatomic, तभी compare करो।

sections.title: Isotope abundance and a gas-mixture average mass

board_events.text: Isotope abundance of element X (JEE Main)
Masses 62.93 and 64.93 u; average 63.55 u. Let ⁶³X fraction = x.
So ⁶³X = 69%, ⁶⁵X = 31%; then in 6.355 g there are 0.100 mol of atoms.
Gas mixture: CH₄ + C₂H₆, average M = 20 (JEE Adv)
In 5 g: n = 0.25 mol; H atoms = 1.143 mol = 6.88×10²³.

segments.text: Two problems that chain averaging with the mole concept. First, an element X with two isotopes.
The masses are sixty two point nine three and sixty four point nine three units, average sixty three point five five. Let the fraction of the lighter isotope be x.
Setting up the weighted average, sixty two point nine three x plus sixty four point nine three times one minus x equals sixty three point five five, which solves to x equals zero point six nine.
So the lighter isotope is sixty nine percent and the heavier thirty one percent, and using the average as molar mass, six point three five five grams is zero point one zero zero moles of atoms.
The number of the lighter isotope atoms is sixty nine percent of the total, four point one six times ten to the twenty two atoms.
<excited>Second, a J E E Advanced mixture of methane and ethane with average molar mass twenty.
Let the mole fraction of methane be a, then sixteen a plus thirty times one minus a equals twenty, which gives a equal to five sevenths.

In five grams the total is zero point two five moles, and counting hydrogen from both molecules gives one point one four three moles, that is six point eight eight times ten to the twenty three hydrogen atoms.
दो problems जो averaging को mole concept से chain करते हैं। पहला, दो isotopes वाला element X.
Masses हैं sixty two point nine three और sixty four point nine three units, average sixty three point five five. हल्के isotope का fraction x मान लो।
Weighted average बनाओ, sixty two point nine three x plus sixty four point nine three गुणा one minus x बराबर sixty three point five five, जो हल होकर x बराबर zero point six nine.
तो हल्का isotope sixty nine percent और भारी thirty one percent, और average को molar mass मानकर, six point three five five grams है zero point one zero zero moles atoms.
हल्के isotope के atoms की संख्या total का sixty nine percent है, four point one six times ten to the twenty two atoms.
<excited>दूसरा, methane और ethane का एक J E E Advanced mixture, average molar mass twenty.
Methane का mole fraction a मान लो, तो sixteen a plus thirty गुणा one minus a बराबर twenty, जिससे a बराबर five sevenths.

पाँच grams में total है zero point two five moles, और दोनों molecules से hydrogen गिनने पर मिलता है one point one four three moles, यानी six point eight eight times ten to the twenty three hydrogen atoms.

sections.title: Mole-concept pitfalls and a no-arithmetic shortcut

board_events.text: Pitfalls in the mole concept
Molecules vs atoms differ by atomicity: 1 mol N₂ = N_A molecules but 2N_A atoms. Read the noun.
Never leap grams → particles; land on moles first, every time.
Average atomic mass is a weighted average — not a real single-atom mass.
22.4 L is a gas-at-STP ticket only — never for solids or liquids.
For 'which has more particles', write each as mass ÷ molar mass (× atomicity) and compare.
Pro-tip: N_A cancels out of every comparison — rank fractions by inspection.

segments.text: Four pitfalls and one shortcut that saves real time in the exam hall.
First, confusing molecules with atoms. One mole of nitrogen gas is Avogadro's number of molecules but twice that many atoms. Always read the noun in the question.
Second, skipping the mole hub. Trying to leap straight from grams to number of particles invites error, land on moles first, every single time.
Third, treating the average atomic mass as real. No chlorine atom weighs thirty five point five units, that figure is a weighted average across isotopes.
Fourth, misapplying twenty two point four litres. It is moles of gas at S T P only, never for liquids or solids, and never forget the S T P convention.
Now the shortcut. For which sample has more particles, never compute full values, just write each as mass divided by molar mass, and for atoms multiply by atomicity.
<whisper>Here is the secret, Avogadro's number cancels out of every comparison, so you can rank four options in under fifteen seconds without ever touching it.
चार pitfalls और एक shortcut जो exam hall में असली समय बचाता है।
पहला, molecules को atoms से confuse करना। एक mole nitrogen gas Avogadro's number molecules है पर उसका दुगना atoms. सवाल में noun हमेशा पढ़ो।
दूसरा, mole hub skip करना। सीधे grams से number of particles पर छलाँग error बुलाती है, हर बार पहले moles पर उतरो।
तीसरा, average atomic mass को real मानना। कोई chlorine atom thirty five point five units का नहीं होता, वो figure isotopes का weighted average है।
चौथा, twenty two point four litres को ग़लत apply करना। ये सिर्फ़ S T P पर gas के moles के लिए है, liquids या solids के लिए कभी नहीं, और S T P convention कभी मत भूलो।
अब shortcut. किस sample में ज़्यादा particles हैं, पूरे values कभी मत निकालो, बस हर एक को mass बटा molar mass लिखो, और atoms के लिए atomicity से गुणा करो।
<whisper>यही secret है, Avogadro's number हर comparison से cancel हो जाता है, तो आप चार options को उसे छुए बिना पंद्रह second से कम में rank कर सकते हो।

sections.title: The nutrition label and the two layers of a recipe

board_events.text: Percentage composition = chemistry's nutrition label
It tells what mass-fraction of a compound is each element.
Empirical formula: the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms (glucose → CH₂O).
Molecular formula: the actual count in one molecule (glucose → C₆H₁₂O₆).
Same empirical CH₂O: formaldehyde (30) vs glucose (180) — molar mass tells them apart.
Ionic compounds (NaCl) have only an empirical formula — no discrete molecule exists.
This is the law of definite proportions expressed as numbers.

segments.text: <curious>Ask a halwai what goes into kaju katli and he says, by weight it's about sixty percent cashew, thirty percent sugar. That breakdown is percentage composition.
For a compound it tells you what mass fraction of the whole is carbon, what fraction is hydrogen, and so on, the chemical nutrition label.
A recipe has two layers, and chemistry mirrors them. The first is the simplest ratio of atoms, the empirical formula, so glucose is C H two O, one carbon to two hydrogen to one oxygen.
The second is the actual count in one real molecule, the molecular formula, and glucose is really C six H twelve O six, six times the empirical unit.
The link between them is a whole number multiplier, the molecular formula equals n times the empirical formula.

This is why empirical formula alone is never enough. Formaldehyde and glucose share the empirical formula C H two O, yet formaldehyde is molar mass thirty and glucose is one eighty. The molar mass tells them apart.
One exception, ionic compounds like sodium chloride have only an empirical formula, because there is no discrete molecule, just a lattice in a fixed ratio.
And notice, this whole idea is simply the law of definite proportions expressed as numbers.
<curious>Halwai से पूछो kaju katli में क्या जाता है, वो कहता है by weight लगभग sixty percent cashew, thirty percent sugar. वही breakdown percentage composition है।
किसी compound के लिए ये बताता है कि पूरे का कितना mass fraction carbon है, कितना hydrogen, वग़ैरह, chemical nutrition label.
एक recipe में दो layers होती हैं, और chemistry उन्हें mirror करती है। पहली है atoms का सबसे simple ratio, empirical formula, तो glucose है C H two O, एक carbon, दो hydrogen, एक oxygen.
दूसरी है एक असली molecule में actual count, molecular formula, और glucose असल में C six H twelve O six है, empirical unit का छह गुना।
इन दोनों के बीच link एक whole number multiplier है, molecular formula बराबर n गुणा empirical formula.

इसीलिए अकेला empirical formula कभी काफ़ी नहीं। Formaldehyde और glucose दोनों का empirical formula C H two O है, फिर भी formaldehyde का molar mass thirty और glucose का one eighty. Molar mass इन्हें अलग करता है।
एक exception, sodium chloride जैसे ionic compounds में सिर्फ़ empirical formula होता है, क्योंकि कोई discrete molecule नहीं, बस एक fixed ratio वाला lattice.
और ध्यान दो, ये पूरा idea बस law of definite proportions है numbers में expressed.

sections.title: The empirical routine, combustion, and the direct method

board_events.text: Empirical formula: the 5-step routine
1. Assume a 100 g sample → each percent becomes grams directly.
2. Divide each mass by its atomic mass → moles (atoms combine by number, not mass).
3. Divide all moles by the smallest. 4. Clear fractions (×2, ×3, ×4). 5. Subscripts.
.5 → ×2, .33/.67 → ×3, .25 → ×4; ignore rounding noise like 1.98.
Combustion: all C → CO₂, all H → H₂O; oxygen by difference.
Direct method (molar mass known): atoms = (% ÷ 100) × molar mass ÷ atomic mass.
Oxygen can't be measured directly — product O comes partly from the air.

segments.text: The skill here is a clean, repeatable routine. Master the empirical formula routine and everything follows.
Step one, assume a hundred gram sample, so every percentage becomes a mass in grams directly, forty percent carbon becomes forty grams.
Step two, divide each element's mass by its atomic mass to get moles, because atoms combine in ratios of number, never mass. This is the step most often skipped.
Step three, divide every mole value by the smallest. Step four, clear stubborn fractions by multiplying the whole set. Step five, write the whole numbers as subscripts.

For clearing fractions, a trailing point five means times two, point three three or point six seven means times three, point two five means times four, but ignore rounding noise like one point nine eight.
For combustion analysis, all the carbon ends up in carbon dioxide and all the hydrogen in water, so back calculate their masses, and find oxygen by difference.
And when the molar mass is known from the start, use the direct method, the atoms of an element equal the percent over one hundred, times molar mass, divided by atomic mass.
One caution on combustion, oxygen cannot be measured directly, because the product oxygen comes partly from the air, so subtraction isolates the compound's own oxygen.
यहाँ skill एक clean, repeatable routine है। Empirical formula routine में महारत हासिल करो और बाक़ी सब follow करता है।
Step one, एक hundred gram sample मान लो, तो हर percentage सीधे grams में mass बन जाता है, forty percent carbon बनता है forty grams.
Step two, हर element का mass उसके atomic mass से भाग दो moles पाने के लिए, क्योंकि atoms number के ratio में combine होते हैं, mass के कभी नहीं। यही step सबसे ज़्यादा छूटता है।
Step three, हर mole value को सबसे छोटे से भाग दो। Step four, ज़िद्दी fractions को पूरे set को गुणा करके clear करो। Step five, whole numbers को subscripts लिखो।

Fractions clear करने के लिए, trailing point five मतलब गुणा two, point three three या point six seven मतलब गुणा three, point two five मतलब गुणा four, पर one point nine eight जैसा rounding noise ignore करो।
Combustion analysis के लिए, सारा carbon carbon dioxide में जाता है और सारा hydrogen water में, तो उनके masses back calculate करो, और oxygen difference से निकालो।
और जब molar mass शुरू से पता हो, direct method इस्तेमाल करो, किसी element के atoms बराबर percent बटा one hundred, गुणा molar mass, बटा atomic mass.
Combustion पर एक caution, oxygen सीधे नहीं नापा जा सकता, क्योंकि product oxygen कुछ हद तक air से आता है, तो subtraction compound के अपने oxygen को अलग करता है।

sections.title: The formula-determination toolkit

board_events.text: Percentage, empirical, molecular — the relations
Ionic compounds: empirical (formula unit) only — no molecular formula.

segments.text: Here is the toolkit for turning composition into a formula.
The mass percent of an element is its count times its atomic mass, over the molar mass, times one hundred.
The multiplier n is the molecular mass over the empirical formula mass, and the molecular formula is n times the empirical formula.
For combustion, the carbon mass is twelve over forty four times the carbon dioxide mass, and the hydrogen mass is two over eighteen times the water mass.
The oxygen mass is then found by difference, the compound mass minus the carbon and hydrogen masses.
For the direct method, the atoms of an element equal the percent over one hundred, times molar mass over atomic mass.
And molar mass is twice the vapour density, the same relation you met in the mole subtopic.
One reminder on the board, ionic compounds have only an empirical formula, the formula unit, and no molecular formula at all.
ये रहा composition को formula में बदलने का toolkit.
किसी element का mass percent है उसका count गुणा atomic mass, बटा molar mass, गुणा one hundred.
Multiplier n है molecular mass बटा empirical formula mass, और molecular formula है n गुणा empirical formula.
Combustion के लिए, carbon mass है twelve बटा forty four गुणा carbon dioxide mass, और hydrogen mass है two बटा eighteen गुणा water mass.
Oxygen mass फिर difference से निकलता है, compound mass minus carbon और hydrogen masses.
Direct method के लिए, किसी element के atoms बराबर percent बटा one hundred, गुणा molar mass बटा atomic mass.
और molar mass vapour density का दुगना है, वही relation जो mole subtopic में मिला था।
Board पर एक reminder, ionic compounds में सिर्फ़ empirical formula होता है, formula unit, और molecular formula बिल्कुल नहीं।

sections.title: Percentage composition and the highest-nitrogen trap

board_events.text: Percentage composition of urea, CO(NH₂)₂
Urea's 46.7% nitrogen is why it's a prized fertiliser.
Which fertiliser has the most nitrogen?
Shortcut: %N = 14×(no. of N)/M × 100 — never compute full composition.
Smallest molar mass with the most N atoms wins.

segments.text: Let's compute a full composition, then learn to skip most of that work. First, the percentage composition of urea.
The molar mass is twelve plus sixteen plus two times, fourteen plus two, which is sixty grams per mole. The molecule has one carbon, one oxygen, two nitrogen, four hydrogen.
So carbon is twenty point zero percent, oxygen twenty six point seven, nitrogen forty six point seven, and hydrogen six point seven, and they sum to about one hundred, a good check.
That high nitrogen content, forty six point seven percent, is exactly why urea is such a prized fertiliser.
<chuckle>Now the speed trap, which nitrogenous fertiliser has the highest nitrogen by mass?
Use the shortcut, percent nitrogen is fourteen times the number of nitrogen atoms, over the molar mass, times one hundred. Never compute the full composition.
Urea gives twenty eight over sixty, forty six point seven percent, beating ammonium nitrate at thirty five, ammonium sulphate at twenty one, and calcium nitrate at seventeen. So urea wins.
The rule of thumb, the smallest molar mass carrying the most nitrogen atoms wins.
एक पूरा composition निकालते हैं, फिर उस काम का ज़्यादातर हिस्सा skip करना सीखते हैं। पहला, urea का percentage composition.
Molar mass है twelve plus sixteen plus two गुणा, fourteen plus two, यानी sixty grams per mole. Molecule में एक carbon, एक oxygen, दो nitrogen, चार hydrogen हैं।
तो carbon twenty point zero percent, oxygen twenty six point seven, nitrogen forty six point seven, और hydrogen six point seven, और इनका sum लगभग one hundred, एक अच्छा check.
वो ऊँचा nitrogen content, forty six point seven percent, ठीक इसीलिए urea इतना prized fertiliser है।
<chuckle>अब speed trap, किस nitrogenous fertiliser में by mass सबसे ज़्यादा nitrogen है?
Shortcut इस्तेमाल करो, percent nitrogen है fourteen गुणा nitrogen atoms की संख्या, बटा molar mass, गुणा one hundred. पूरा composition कभी मत निकालो।
Urea देता है twenty eight बटा sixty, forty six point seven percent, ammonium nitrate thirty five, ammonium sulphate twenty one, और calcium nitrate seventeen को हराते हुए। तो urea जीतता है।
Rule of thumb, सबसे कम molar mass जिसमें सबसे ज़्यादा nitrogen atoms हों, वही जीतता है।

sections.title: Combustion to molecular formula, and a hydrate

board_events.text: Combustion → molecular formula (JEE Main)
0.60 g compound → 0.88 g CO₂, 0.36 g H₂O; molar mass 60.
Hydrate MgSO₄·xH₂O loses 51.2% water
x must be an integer: MgSO₄·7H₂O (Epsom salt).

segments.text: Two problems that chain the whole routine. First, combustion analysis giving a molecular formula.
Zero point six grams of a compound with carbon, hydrogen and oxygen burns to give zero point eight eight grams of carbon dioxide and zero point three six grams of water, molar mass sixty.

The carbon mass is twelve over forty four of the carbon dioxide, zero point two four grams, the hydrogen is two over eighteen of the water, zero point zero four grams, and oxygen by difference is zero point three two grams.
Converting to moles gives zero point zero two, zero point zero four, zero point zero two, a ratio of one to two to one, so the empirical formula is C H two O with mass thirty.
The multiplier n is sixty over thirty, which is two, so the molecular formula is C two H four O two, acetic acid.
<excited>Second, a J E E Advanced hydrate. Magnesium sulphate dot x water loses fifty one point two percent of its mass as water.
Set up the mass fraction, eighteen x over one twenty plus eighteen x equals zero point five one two, which solves to x equals six point nine nine.
And x must be an integer, a formula cannot hold six point nine nine waters, so x is seven, the salt is magnesium sulphate dot seven water, Epsom salt.
दो problems जो पूरी routine को chain करते हैं। पहला, combustion analysis जो molecular formula देता है।
Zero point six grams का एक compound जिसमें carbon, hydrogen और oxygen हैं, जलकर zero point eight eight grams carbon dioxide और zero point three six grams water देता है, molar mass sixty.

Carbon mass carbon dioxide का twelve बटा forty four है, zero point two four grams, hydrogen water का two बटा eighteen है, zero point zero four grams, और oxygen difference से zero point three two grams.
Moles में बदलने पर मिलता है zero point zero two, zero point zero four, zero point zero two, ratio one to two to one, तो empirical formula है C H two O mass thirty के साथ।
Multiplier n है sixty बटा thirty, यानी two, तो molecular formula है C two H four O two, acetic acid.
<excited>दूसरा, एक J E E Advanced hydrate. Magnesium sulphate dot x water अपने mass का fifty one point two percent water के रूप में खोता है।
Mass fraction बनाओ, eighteen x बटा one twenty plus eighteen x बराबर zero point five one two, जो हल होकर x बराबर six point nine nine.
और x एक integer होना चाहिए, कोई formula six point nine nine water नहीं रख सकता, तो x है seven, salt है magnesium sulphate dot seven water, Epsom salt.

sections.title: Formula pitfalls and the 100-gram trick

board_events.text: Empirical/molecular formula pitfalls
Taking ratios of mass instead of moles — the single biggest error. Divide by atomic mass first.
Rounding away genuine fractions: .5, .33, .25 are real — multiply by 2, 3, 4.
Stopping at the empirical formula when a molar mass is given — compute n and multiply.
Combustion oxygen is found by difference, never measured directly.
The 100 g trick: percentages become grams instantly.
Pro-tip: run the sanity check — element masses must sum back to the total.

segments.text: Four pitfalls and two habits to keep formula work clean.
First, taking ratios of mass instead of moles, the single biggest empirical formula error. Mass ratios are meaningless, divide by atomic mass to reach moles first.

Second, rounding away genuine fractions. A ratio ending in point five, point three three, or point two five is real, multiply the whole set by two, three, or four, and only ignore rounding noise like one point nine eight.
Third, stopping at the empirical formula. If a molar mass or vapour density is given, the question wants the molecular formula, so compute n and multiply.
Fourth, measuring combustion oxygen directly. It must be found by difference, because product oxygen includes oxygen from the air.
Now the first habit, the hundred gram trick removes all percentage clutter, percentages become grams instantly.
<whisper>And the second, always run the sanity check, your element masses must sum back to the total. If they do not, you have lost an element, often the oxygen you were meant to find by difference.
चार pitfalls और दो आदतें ताकि formula का काम साफ़ रहे।
पहला, moles की जगह mass के ratios लेना, सबसे बड़ी empirical formula error. Mass ratios बेमतलब हैं, पहले atomic mass से भाग देकर moles तक पहुँचो।

दूसरा, genuine fractions को round करके उड़ा देना। Point five, point three three, या point two five पर ख़त्म होता ratio असली है, पूरे set को two, three, या four से गुणा करो, और सिर्फ़ one point nine eight जैसा rounding noise ignore करो।
तीसरा, empirical formula पर रुक जाना। अगर molar mass या vapour density दिया है, सवाल molecular formula चाहता है, तो n निकालो और गुणा करो।
चौथा, combustion oxygen सीधे नापना। इसे difference से निकालना होता है, क्योंकि product oxygen में air का oxygen शामिल है।
अब पहली आदत, hundred gram trick सारा percentage clutter हटा देता है, percentages तुरंत grams बन जाते हैं।
<whisper>और दूसरी, हमेशा sanity check चलाओ, आपके element masses total में वापस add होने चाहिए। अगर नहीं होते, तो कोई element खो गया, अक्सर वही oxygen जो difference से निकालना था।

sections.title: The balanced equation as a recipe

board_events.text: Coefficients give a MOLE recipe, not a mass recipe
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O reads '2 moles H₂ react with 1 mole O₂'.
So convert given → moles, use the coefficient ratio, then convert back.
Dhaba thali: 2 rotis + 1 bowl dal each. 10 rotis but 3 dals → only 3 thalis.
Dal runs out first = limiting reagent; leftover rotis = excess.
The recipe gives the maximum: the theoretical yield.
Real reactions lose product, so actual yield is usually less.

segments.text: A balanced chemical equation is a recipe, and reading these recipe ratios is called stoichiometry.
When you read two hydrogen plus oxygen gives two water, it means two moles of hydrogen react with one mole of oxygen, not two grams.
So every problem flows the same way, convert what you are given into moles, use the coefficient ratio to find moles of what you want, then convert back to grams, litres, or particles.
<curious>Picture a dhaba recipe, two rotis and one bowl of dal per thali. You have ten rotis but only three bowls of dal, how many thalis?
The dal runs out first, so you serve only three thalis with four rotis left over. The dal is the limiting reagent, and the leftover rotis are in excess.
The recipe also gives the maximum possible product, the theoretical yield.
The percentage yield measures efficiency, the actual yield over the theoretical yield, times one hundred.
Real reactions lose some product to side reactions and spillage, so the actual yield is usually less than the theoretical.
एक balanced chemical equation एक recipe है, और इन recipe ratios को पढ़ना stoichiometry कहलाता है।
जब आप पढ़ते हो two hydrogen plus oxygen देता है two water, इसका मतलब दो moles hydrogen एक mole oxygen से react करते हैं, दो grams नहीं।
तो हर problem एक ही तरह बहती है, जो दिया है उसे moles में बदलो, जो चाहिए उसके moles के लिए coefficient ratio इस्तेमाल करो, फिर grams, litres, या particles में वापस बदलो।
<curious>एक dhaba recipe सोचो, हर thali पर दो roti और एक bowl dal. आपके पास दस roti हैं पर सिर्फ़ तीन bowl dal, कितनी thali?
Dal पहले ख़त्म होती है, तो आप सिर्फ़ तीन thali परोसते हो और चार roti बच जाती हैं। Dal limiting reagent है, और बची roti excess में हैं।
Recipe maximum possible product भी देती है, theoretical yield.
Percentage yield efficiency नापती है, actual yield बटा theoretical yield, गुणा one hundred.
असली reactions side reactions और spillage में कुछ product खोती हैं, तो actual yield आमतौर पर theoretical से कम होती है।

sections.title: The mole method, POAC, and finding the limiting reagent

board_events.text: Balance → moles → ratio → back
Mole method: balance, convert to moles, apply coefficient ratio, convert to the target unit.
POAC: atoms conserved, e.g. 3×mol(KClO₃) = 2×mol(O₂), no balancing needed.
Limiting reagent: divide each reactant's moles by its coefficient; smallest quotient wins.

board_events.caption: Divide by the coefficient — smallest quotient is limiting

board_events.text: Excess left = supplied − consumed (consumed from the limiting reagent).
Gas-volume on-ramp: volume ratio = coefficient ratio (Avogadro), work in litres directly.
Solution on-ramp: moles = molarity × volume in litres.

segments.text: The spine of every stoichiometry problem is four steps, balance, then moles, then ratio, then back.
The mole method, balance the equation, convert the given quantity to moles, apply the coefficient ratio, and convert to the requested unit.
A faster route for messy equations is the principle of atom conservation, P O A C. Atoms are conserved, so three times moles of potassium chlorate equals two times moles of oxygen, with no balancing.
For the limiting reagent, divide each reactant's moles by its coefficient, and the smallest quotient marks the limiting reagent.
Here it is on the board, dividing by the coefficient puts every reactant on the same per recipe footing, so the smallest quotient runs out first.
The excess left is the supplied moles minus the consumed moles, where consumed is computed from the limiting reagent.
For gases at constant conditions, the volume ratio equals the coefficient ratio by Avogadro, so you can work in litres directly without converting to moles.
And for reactions in solution, the moles of a dissolved reactant are the molarity times the volume in litres, then apply the coefficient ratio as usual.
हर stoichiometry problem की रीढ़ चार steps हैं, balance, फिर moles, फिर ratio, फिर back.
Mole method, equation balance करो, दी गई quantity को moles में बदलो, coefficient ratio apply करो, और माँगी गई unit में बदलो।
उलझी equations के लिए तेज़ रास्ता है principle of atom conservation, P O A C. Atoms conserved होते हैं, तो three गुणा moles potassium chlorate बराबर two गुणा moles oxygen, बिना balancing के।
Limiting reagent के लिए, हर reactant के moles को उसके coefficient से भाग दो, और सबसे छोटा quotient limiting reagent है।
ये रहा board पर, coefficient से भाग देना हर reactant को same per recipe footing पर रखता है, तो सबसे छोटा quotient पहले ख़त्म होता है।
बचा excess है supplied moles minus consumed moles, जहाँ consumed limiting reagent से निकाला जाता है।
Constant conditions पर gases के लिए, volume ratio Avogadro से coefficient ratio के बराबर है, तो आप moles में बदले बिना सीधे litres में काम कर सकते हो।
और solution में reactions के लिए, किसी dissolved reactant के moles हैं molarity गुणा volume in litres, फिर हमेशा की तरह coefficient ratio apply करो।

sections.title: The stoichiometry toolkit

board_events.text: Mole ratio, limiting reagent, yield

board_events.latex: \frac{\text{moles of A}}{\text{coeff of A}} = \frac{\text{moles of B}}{\text{coeff of B}}

board_events.text: Limiting reagent: the reactant with the smallest (moles ÷ coefficient).
POAC: 3·n(KClO₃) = 2·n(O₂) — atoms conserved, no balancing.

segments.text: Here is the stoichiometry toolkit at a glance.
The master relation, moles of A over the coefficient of A equals moles of B over the coefficient of B.
The limiting reagent is the reactant with the smallest value of moles divided by coefficient.
The excess left is the supplied moles minus the consumed moles.
The percentage yield is the actual yield over the theoretical yield, times one hundred.
For a gas at S T P, the moles equal the volume over twenty two point four litres.
For a solution, the moles of solute equal the molarity times the volume in litres.
And the atom conservation shortcut, three times moles of potassium chlorate equals two times moles of oxygen, since atoms are conserved without balancing.
ये रहा stoichiometry toolkit एक नज़र में।
Master relation, moles of A बटा coefficient of A बराबर moles of B बटा coefficient of B.
Limiting reagent वो reactant है जिसका moles बटा coefficient सबसे छोटा हो।
बचा excess है supplied moles minus consumed moles.
Percentage yield है actual yield बटा theoretical yield, गुणा one hundred.
S T P पर gas के लिए, moles बराबर volume बटा twenty two point four litres.
Solution के लिए, solute के moles बराबर molarity गुणा volume in litres.
और atom conservation shortcut, three गुणा moles potassium chlorate बराबर two गुणा moles oxygen, क्योंकि atoms बिना balancing conserved होते हैं।

sections.title: A mass-to-mass calculation and the limiting-reagent trap

board_events.text: CO₂ from 50 g of CaCO₃
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂; M(CaCO₃)=100, so n = 0.50 mol.
Limiting reagent: 2 mol H₂, 1.5 mol O₂
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Divide by coefficient: H₂ = 2/2 = 1; O₂ = 1.5/1 = 1.5.
Not 'more moles of H₂ so O₂ limiting' — divide by the coefficient first.

segments.text: Two examples that build the core discipline. First, a straightforward mass to mass calculation.
Calcium carbonate decomposes to calcium oxide and carbon dioxide. Its molar mass is one hundred, so fifty grams is zero point five moles.
The ratio is one to one, so carbon dioxide is also zero point five moles, and its mass is zero point five times forty four, twenty two grams.
<chuckle>Second, the limiting reagent trap, two moles of hydrogen and one point five moles of oxygen forming water.
The equation is two hydrogen plus oxygen gives two water. Divide by the coefficient, hydrogen is two over two, which is one, and oxygen is one point five over one, which is one point five.
The smallest quotient is hydrogen, so hydrogen is limiting, and the water formed is fixed by hydrogen, two moles.
The trap is seeing more moles of hydrogen and wrongly calling oxygen limiting. Always divide by the coefficient first, raw mole counts are meaningless.
दो examples जो core discipline बनाते हैं। पहला, एक सीधा mass to mass calculation.
Calcium carbonate decompose होकर calcium oxide और carbon dioxide देता है। इसका molar mass one hundred है, तो fifty grams है zero point five moles.
Ratio one to one है, तो carbon dioxide भी zero point five moles, और इसका mass है zero point five गुणा forty four, twenty two grams.
<chuckle>दूसरा, limiting reagent trap, दो moles hydrogen और one point five moles oxygen water बनाते हुए।
Equation है two hydrogen plus oxygen देता है two water. Coefficient से भाग दो, hydrogen है two बटा two, यानी one, और oxygen है one point five बटा one, यानी one point five.
सबसे छोटा quotient hydrogen है, तो hydrogen limiting है, और बना water hydrogen से fix होता है, दो moles.
Trap ये है कि hydrogen के ज़्यादा moles देखकर ग़लती से oxygen को limiting कह देना। हमेशा पहले coefficient से भाग दो, raw mole counts बेमतलब हैं।

sections.title: Mass, excess, and percentage yield in ammonia synthesis

board_events.text: 28 g N₂ + 9 g H₂ → NH₃ (JEE Main)
n(N₂)=1.0, n(H₂)=4.5. Divide: N₂ = 1.0, H₂ = 1.5 → N₂ limiting.
Excess H₂: consumed 3×1.0 = 6 g; supplied 9 g; left 3 g.
50 g N₂ + 10 g H₂, actual NH₃ = 40 g (JEE Adv)
n(N₂)=1.79, n(H₂)=5.0. Divide: 1.79 vs 1.67 → H₂ limiting.

segments.text: Two ammonia problems that show the full discipline, everything anchored on the limiting reagent.
First, twenty eight grams of nitrogen and nine grams of hydrogen. Moles are one and four point five, dividing by coefficients gives one and one point five, so nitrogen is limiting.
Ammonia is two times the nitrogen moles, two moles, which is thirty four grams.
For the excess hydrogen, consumed is three times one, six grams, supplied is nine grams, so three grams of hydrogen are left.
<excited>Second, a J E E Advanced yield problem, fifty grams of nitrogen and ten grams of hydrogen, with forty grams of ammonia actually produced.
Moles are one point seven nine and five, dividing by coefficients gives one point seven nine versus one point six seven, so this time hydrogen is limiting.
The theoretical yield is five times two thirds times seventeen, fifty six point seven grams.
So the percentage yield is forty over fifty six point seven, times one hundred, seventy point six percent. The limiting reagent must be found before the theoretical yield, or the maximum is wrong.
दो ammonia problems जो पूरी discipline दिखाते हैं, सब कुछ limiting reagent पर anchored.
पहला, twenty eight grams nitrogen और nine grams hydrogen. Moles हैं one और four point five, coefficients से भाग देने पर one और one point five, तो nitrogen limiting है।
Ammonia nitrogen moles का दुगना है, दो moles, यानी thirty four grams.
Excess hydrogen के लिए, consumed है three गुणा one, six grams, supplied nine grams, तो three grams hydrogen बचता है।
<excited>दूसरा, एक J E E Advanced yield problem, fifty grams nitrogen और ten grams hydrogen, forty grams ammonia असल में बनते हुए।
Moles हैं one point seven nine और five, coefficients से भाग देने पर one point seven nine versus one point six seven, तो इस बार hydrogen limiting है।
Theoretical yield है five गुणा two thirds गुणा seventeen, fifty six point seven grams.
तो percentage yield है forty बटा fifty six point seven, गुणा one hundred, seventy point six percent. Limiting reagent theoretical yield से पहले निकालना ज़रूरी है, वरना maximum ग़लत आता है।

sections.title: Stoichiometry pitfalls and anchoring on the limiter

board_events.text: Stoichiometry pitfalls
Skipping the balancing step — coefficient ratios only work for a balanced equation.
Ratioing grams — the equation speaks in moles; convert masses/volumes first.
Comparing raw moles for the limiting reagent — divide by the coefficient first.
All product and yield calculations anchor on the limiting reagent, never the excess.
Conservation of mass is a free check: reactant mass in = product mass out.
Pro-tip: write moles above each coefficient — the smallest ratio drives everything.

segments.text: Four pitfalls and a habit that turns multi-part problems into one-line steps.
First, skipping the balancing step. Coefficient ratios are only valid for a balanced equation, so balance first, every time.
Second, ratioing grams. The equation speaks in moles, so convert masses and volumes to moles before applying any ratio.
Third, comparing raw moles for the limiting reagent. Always divide moles by the coefficient first, the smallest quotient is limiting, not the smallest mole count.
Fourth, anchoring product on the wrong reactant. All product and yield calculations must be based on the limiting reagent, never the one in excess.
And a free check, conservation of mass, the total reactant mass in equals the total product mass out.

<excited>Here is the pro-tip, write each reactant's moles directly above its coefficient and read the ratio in one glance. That single smallest number then drives product mass, excess left, and yield.
चार pitfalls और एक आदत जो multi-part problems को one-line steps में बदल देती है।
पहला, balancing step skip करना। Coefficient ratios सिर्फ़ balanced equation के लिए valid हैं, तो हर बार पहले balance करो।
दूसरा, grams का ratio लेना। Equation moles में बोलती है, तो कोई भी ratio apply करने से पहले masses और volumes को moles में बदलो।
तीसरा, limiting reagent के लिए raw moles compare करना। हमेशा पहले moles को coefficient से भाग दो, सबसे छोटा quotient limiting है, सबसे छोटा mole count नहीं।
चौथा, product को ग़लत reactant पर anchor करना। सारे product और yield calculations limiting reagent पर आधारित होने चाहिए, excess वाले पर कभी नहीं।
और एक free check, conservation of mass, कुल reactant mass in बराबर कुल product mass out.
<excited>ये है pro-tip, हर reactant के moles सीधे उसके coefficient के ऊपर लिखो और ratio एक नज़र में पढ़ो। वही एक सबसे छोटा number फिर product mass, बचा excess, और yield सब चलाता है।

sections.title: How crowded are the particles? And what you divide by

board_events.text: Concentration = how crowded the dissolved particles are
Molarity (M): moles solute ÷ volume of solution — the lab workhorse.
Molality (m): moles solute ÷ mass of solvent.
Mole fraction (x): moles of one component ÷ total moles.
Mass % and ppm: solute as a fraction of total mass (ppm for very dilute).
Local train: passengers per coach (volume) drifts on a hot day; per tonne (mass) never does.
Volume-based (molarity, normality, formality) drift with temperature.
Mass/mole-based (molality, mole fraction, mass %) are rock-steady.

segments.text: <curious>Two people make nimbu paani, one stirs in two spoons of sugar, the other six. Same drink, different strength. Concentration answers how crowded the dissolved particles are.

There are several honest ways to measure that crowding, differing in what you divide by. Molarity is moles of solute over the volume of solution, the lab workhorse, because you measure liquids by volume.
Molality is moles of solute over the mass of solvent.
Mole fraction is the moles of one component over the total moles of everything.
And you can express the solute as a fraction of total mass, mass percent, or for very dilute solutions, parts per million.

Now the key intuition. Picture a crowded local train, passengers per coach is a fixed volume, but on a hot day the metal coach expands a hair, so that ratio drifts, while passengers per tonne never does.
So anything defined using volume, molarity, normality, formality, drifts with temperature, because liquids expand when heated.
But anything defined using mass or moles, molality, mole fraction, mass percent, is rock steady, whatever the temperature.
<curious>दो लोग nimbu paani बनाते हैं, एक दो spoon sugar डालता है, दूसरा छह। Same drink, अलग strength. Concentration बताता है dissolved particles कितने crowded हैं।
उस crowding को नापने के कई ईमानदार तरीक़े हैं, फ़र्क़ इसमें कि आप किससे भाग देते हो। Molarity है moles solute बटा volume of solution, lab workhorse, क्योंकि liquids को volume से नापते हैं।
Molality है moles solute बटा mass of solvent.
Mole fraction है किसी एक component के moles बटा सबके total moles.
और solute को total mass के fraction के रूप में लिख सकते हो, mass percent, या बहुत dilute solutions के लिए, parts per million.
अब key intuition. एक crowded local train सोचो, passengers per coach एक fixed volume है, पर गरम दिन पर metal coach ज़रा फैलता है, तो वो ratio drift करता है, जबकि passengers per tonne कभी नहीं।
तो volume से define कोई भी चीज़, molarity, normality, formality, temperature के साथ drift करती है, क्योंकि liquids गरम होने पर फैलते हैं।
पर mass या moles से define कोई भी चीज़, molality, mole fraction, mass percent, rock steady है, temperature चाहे जो हो।

sections.title: Building concentrations, interconverting, and diluting

board_events.text: The denominator IS the identity of the term
Build any term: moles solute, then divide — solution volume, solvent mass, or total moles.
Mass % → molarity needs density: only density bridges mass to volume.
Molality ↔ molarity also needs density (one is per-volume, the other per-mass).
Dilution: adding solvent keeps moles fixed, so M₁V₁ = M₂V₂.
Water to add = V₂ − V₁, using the FINAL total volume.
Normality: N = (n-factor) × M; for H₂SO₄ (basicity 2), N = 2M.
Ion molarity: 0.2 M CaCl₂ is 0.2 M in Ca²⁺ but 0.4 M in Cl⁻.

segments.text: The definitions are simple, the marks are won in interconversion and in which mass goes where.
To build any concentration, get the moles of solute, then divide by the correct denominator, the solution volume for molarity, the solvent mass for molality, the total moles for mole fraction.
To go from mass percent to molarity you need the density, because mass percent knows nothing about volume, and only density bridges mass to volume.
The same is true converting between molality and molarity, one term is per volume and the other per mass, so density is the only quantity that relates a solution's mass to its volume.
For dilution, adding pure solvent leaves the moles of solute unchanged, so molarity one times volume one equals molarity two times volume two.
And a classic trap, the water to add is the final volume minus the initial volume, because the formula uses the final total volume.
For normality, multiply molarity by the n factor, so sulphuric acid with basicity two has normality equal to twice its molarity.

And when a salt dissociates, the ion molarity is the salt molarity times the number of those ions, so zero point two molar calcium chloride is zero point two molar in calcium but zero point four molar in chloride.
Definitions simple हैं, marks interconversion में और इसमें बनते हैं कि कौन सा mass कहाँ जाता है।
कोई भी concentration बनाने के लिए, solute के moles निकालो, फिर सही denominator से भाग दो, molarity के लिए solution volume, molality के लिए solvent mass, mole fraction के लिए total moles.
Mass percent से molarity पर जाने के लिए density चाहिए, क्योंकि mass percent को volume का कुछ पता नहीं, और सिर्फ़ density mass को volume से जोड़ती है।
यही molality और molarity के बीच convert करने में सच है, एक term per volume है और दूसरा per mass, तो density ही एकमात्र quantity है जो solution के mass को उसके volume से जोड़ती है।
Dilution के लिए, pure solvent डालने से solute के moles वैसे ही रहते हैं, तो molarity one गुणा volume one बराबर molarity two गुणा volume two.
और एक classic trap, डालने वाला water है final volume minus initial volume, क्योंकि formula final total volume इस्तेमाल करता है।
Normality के लिए, molarity को n factor से गुणा करो, तो basicity two वाले sulphuric acid की normality उसकी molarity का दुगना है।

और जब कोई salt dissociate होता है, ion molarity है salt molarity गुणा उन ions की संख्या, तो zero point two molar calcium chloride, calcium में zero point two molar पर chloride में zero point four molar है।

sections.title: The concentration toolkit

board_events.text: Every concentration term at a glance

board_events.latex: M = \frac{\text{mol solute}}{\text{L solution}},\qquad m = \frac{\text{mol solute}}{\text{kg solvent}}
M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2,\qquad M_R = \frac{\sum M_i V_i}{\sum V_i}

board_events.text: Volume drifts with T; mass/mole terms don't. No density, no M ↔ m.

segments.text: Here is every concentration term on one board.
Mass percent is mass of solute over mass of solution times one hundred, and parts per million is the same ratio times ten to the sixth.
Mole fraction of a component is its moles over the total moles, and the mole fractions add to one.
Molarity is moles of solute per litre of solution, while molality is moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.
Normality is the n factor times the molarity.
For dilution, molarity one times volume one equals molarity two times volume two, and for mixing, the resulting molarity is the sum of each molarity times volume, over the total volume.
And molarity from mass percent is ten times density times the mass percent, over the solute molar mass, with density in gram per millilitre.
Remember the theme, volume based terms drift with temperature while mass and mole terms do not, and there is no converting between molarity and molality without the density.
ये रहा हर concentration term एक board पर।
Mass percent है mass of solute बटा mass of solution गुणा one hundred, और parts per million वही ratio गुणा ten to the sixth.
किसी component का mole fraction है उसके moles बटा total moles, और mole fractions जुड़कर one बनते हैं।
Molarity है moles of solute प्रति litre of solution, जबकि molality है moles of solute प्रति kilogram of solvent.
Normality है n factor गुणा molarity.
Dilution के लिए, molarity one गुणा volume one बराबर molarity two गुणा volume two, और mixing के लिए, resulting molarity है हर molarity गुणा volume का sum, बटा total volume.
और mass percent से molarity है ten गुणा density गुणा mass percent, बटा solute molar mass, density gram per millilitre में।
Theme याद रखो, volume based terms temperature के साथ drift करते हैं जबकि mass और mole terms नहीं, और density के बिना molarity और molality के बीच conversion नहीं होता।

sections.title: Molarity, and the temperature-independent term

board_events.text: Molarity of 5.85 g NaCl in 500 mL solution
Which term is temperature-independent?
Molarity, normality, formality are per-litre-of-solution → volume-based.
Only molality is per-kg-of-solvent → mass-based → temperature-proof.
Scan the denominator: a volume → T-dependent; a mass → T-independent.

segments.text: Two examples, one a calculation, one a reasoning trap. First, the molarity of a salt solution.
Dissolve five point eight five grams of sodium chloride, molar mass fifty eight point five, so the moles are zero point one zero zero.
The volume is five hundred millilitres, half a litre, so molarity is zero point one over zero point five, which is zero point two zero zero moles per litre.
<chuckle>Second, a N E E T style trap, which concentration term is independent of temperature?
Do not recall the definitions one by one, apply the rule. Molarity, normality and formality are all per litre of solution, so they are volume based.
Only molality is per kilogram of solvent, so it is mass based and therefore temperature proof. The answer is molality.
The habit that wins this, scan the denominator, see a volume and it is temperature dependent, see a mass and it is temperature independent.
दो examples, एक calculation, एक reasoning trap. पहला, एक salt solution की molarity.
पाँच point आठ पाँच grams sodium chloride घोलो, molar mass fifty eight point five, तो moles हैं zero point one zero zero.
Volume है five hundred millilitres, आधा litre, तो molarity है zero point one बटा zero point five, यानी zero point two zero zero moles per litre.
<chuckle>दूसरा, एक N E E T style trap, कौन सा concentration term temperature से independent है?
Definitions एक एक करके याद मत करो, rule apply करो। Molarity, normality और formality सब per litre of solution हैं, तो वो volume based हैं।
सिर्फ़ molality per kilogram of solvent है, तो वो mass based है और इसलिए temperature proof. Answer है molality.
जो आदत इसे जिताती है, denominator scan करो, volume दिखे तो temperature dependent, mass दिखे तो temperature independent.

sections.title: Molality to molarity with density, and a mixing-dilution chain

board_events.text: 2.0 molal, M(solute)=50, density 1.05 (JEE Main)
2.0 mol solute per 1000 g solvent → solute mass 100 g → solution mass 1100 g.
Without density, solution mass could never become a volume.
Mix + dilute H₂SO₄, then find normality (JEE Adv)
Dilution uses the FINAL volume, not the sum of mixed volumes.

segments.text: Two harder problems where density and the final-volume rule do the real work. First, converting molality to molarity.
A two molal solution means two moles of solute per one thousand grams of solvent, so the solute mass is one hundred grams, and the solution mass is eleven hundred grams.

Using the density one point zero five, the volume is eleven hundred over one point zero five, one thousand forty seven point six millilitres, so the molarity is two over one point zero four seven six, one point nine one molar.
Notice the density is doing the essential work, without it the solution mass could never become a volume.
<excited>Second, a mixing then dilution problem with sulphuric acid, and then its normality.
The mixed moles are zero point zero five plus zero point zero three, zero point zero eight moles, and the final volume is five hundred millilitres, so the molarity is zero point one six.
The normality is the n factor two times zero point one six, zero point three two normal, since sulphuric acid has basicity two.
The subtle step, the dilution quietly uses the final volume, five hundred millilitres, not the sum of the two mixed volumes.
दो कठिन problems जहाँ density और final-volume rule असली काम करते हैं। पहला, molality को molarity में बदलना।
एक two molal solution का मतलब दो moles solute प्रति one thousand grams solvent, तो solute mass one hundred grams, और solution mass eleven hundred grams.

Density one point zero five से, volume है eleven hundred बटा one point zero five, one thousand forty seven point six millilitres, तो molarity है two बटा one point zero four seven six, one point nine one molar.
ध्यान दो density ही असली काम कर रही है, इसके बिना solution mass कभी volume नहीं बन सकता था।
<excited>दूसरा, sulphuric acid के साथ mixing फिर dilution का problem, और फिर उसकी normality.
Mixed moles हैं zero point zero five plus zero point zero three, zero point zero eight moles, और final volume है five hundred millilitres, तो molarity है zero point one six.
Normality है n factor two गुणा zero point one six, zero point three two normal, क्योंकि sulphuric acid की basicity two है।
Subtle step, dilution चुपके से final volume इस्तेमाल करता है, five hundred millilitres, दोनों mixed volumes के sum को नहीं।

sections.title: Concentration pitfalls and the fixed-anchor trick

board_events.text: Concentration pitfalls
Solvent mass vs solution mass: molality uses solvent; mass % and density use solution.
Assuming molarity = molality — true only for very dilute aqueous solutions.
Dilution trap: M₁V₁ = M₂V₂ uses the final volume, so water added = V₂ − V₁.
Normality n-factor: H₂SO₄ at 0.16 M is 0.32 N, not 0.16 N.
Anchor on a fixed amount: 1000 g solvent for molality, 100 g solution for mass %.
Pro-tip: fix the anchor and every other quantity follows in one step.

segments.text: Four pitfalls and one anchor habit that keeps interconversions painless.
First, solvent mass versus solution mass. Molality is per kilogram of solvent, while mass percent and density use the solution, so read which one the problem gives and never substitute.
Second, assuming molarity equals molality. They coincide only for very dilute aqueous solutions, otherwise you need the density.
Third, the dilution volume trap. Molarity one times volume one equals molarity two times volume two uses the final total volume, so the water added is the final volume minus the initial volume.
Fourth, forgetting the n factor for normality. Sulphuric acid at zero point one six molar is zero point three two normal, not zero point one six.
Now the habit, for any density interconversion anchor on a fixed, convenient amount, one thousand grams of solvent for molality, one hundred grams of solution for mass percent.
<whisper>Here is the pro-tip, once you fix that anchor, every other quantity follows by a single multiplication or division, and you never lose track of which mass is which.
चार pitfalls और एक anchor आदत जो interconversions को आसान रखती है।
पहला, solvent mass versus solution mass. Molality per kilogram of solvent है, जबकि mass percent और density solution इस्तेमाल करते हैं, तो पढ़ो problem कौन सा देता है और कभी substitute मत करो।
दूसरा, molarity को molality मान लेना। ये सिर्फ़ बहुत dilute aqueous solutions में मिलते हैं, वरना density चाहिए।
तीसरा, dilution volume trap. Molarity one गुणा volume one बराबर molarity two गुणा volume two final total volume इस्तेमाल करता है, तो डाला गया water है final volume minus initial volume.
चौथा, normality के लिए n factor भूलना। Sulphuric acid zero point one six molar पर zero point three two normal है, zero point one six नहीं।
अब आदत, किसी भी density interconversion के लिए एक fixed, convenient amount पर anchor करो, molality के लिए one thousand grams solvent, mass percent के लिए one hundred grams solution.
<whisper>ये है pro-tip, एक बार वो anchor fix कर लो, हर बाक़ी quantity एक ही multiplication या division से आ जाती है, और आप कभी नहीं भूलते कौन सा mass कौन सा है।

sections.title: Your complete toolkit for the chapter

board_events.text: The whole chapter's formulas in one place

board_events.latex: M = \frac{\text{mol solute}}{\text{L soln}},\quad m = \frac{\text{mol solute}}{\text{kg solvent}}
M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2,\qquad N = (\text{n-factor})\times M

segments.text: Here is your complete toolkit, the whole chapter's formulas gathered in one place, just to fix them in memory.
From measurement, density is mass over volume, and kelvin is Celsius plus two seven three point one five.
The mole triangle, moles equal mass over molar mass, equal number over Avogadro's number, equal volume over twenty two point four litres at S T P.
Average atomic mass is the abundance weighted mean, and molar mass is twice the vapour density.
For formulas, the multiplier n is the molecular mass over the empirical formula mass, and the molecular formula is n times the empirical formula.
For stoichiometry, moles of A over coefficient of A equals moles of B over coefficient of B, and percentage yield is actual over theoretical, times one hundred.
For concentration, molarity is moles per litre of solution and molality is moles per kilogram of solvent.
And finally, dilution is molarity one volume one equals molarity two volume two, and normality is the n factor times molarity. That is the whole toolkit.
ये रहा आपका complete toolkit, पूरे chapter के formulas एक जगह इकट्ठा, बस इन्हें memory में fix करने के लिए।
Measurement से, density है mass over volume, और kelvin है Celsius plus two seven three point one five.
Mole triangle, moles बराबर mass over molar mass, बराबर number over Avogadro's number, बराबर volume over twenty two point four litres S T P पर।
Average atomic mass abundance weighted mean है, और molar mass vapour density का दुगना।
Formulas के लिए, multiplier n है molecular mass over empirical formula mass, और molecular formula है n गुणा empirical formula.
Stoichiometry के लिए, moles of A over coefficient of A बराबर moles of B over coefficient of B, और percentage yield है actual over theoretical, गुणा one hundred.
Concentration के लिए, molarity है moles per litre of solution और molality है moles per kilogram of solvent.
और आख़िर में, dilution है molarity one volume one बराबर molarity two volume two, और normality है n factor गुणा molarity. यही पूरा toolkit है।

segments.text: Let's finish with a quick recall sweep across the whole chapter, one board to revise from.
Matter splits into pure substances, elements and compounds, and mixtures, homogeneous and heterogeneous, and the one test for change type is, was a new substance formed?
For measurement, a quantity is a number times a unit, one metre cubed is ten to the sixth centimetre cubed, and kelvin is Celsius plus two seven three point one five.
For significant figures, leading zeros never count, trailing zeros count only with a decimal, addition follows decimal places, and multiplication follows significant figures.
The five laws are conservation, definite, multiple, and reciprocal proportions, and combining volumes, with Avogadro giving volume proportional to moles.

For the mole, Avogadro's number is six point zero two two times ten to the twenty three, moles equal mass over molar mass, number over Avogadro's number, or volume over twenty two point four, and average atomic mass is a weighted mean.
For formulas, convert mass to moles before any ratio, the molecular formula is n times the empirical formula, and oxygen is found by difference in combustion.

And for stoichiometry, the spine is balance, mole, ratio, back, the limiting reagent is the smallest moles over coefficient, and remember molarity drifts with temperature while molality does not. That is the chapter.
पूरे chapter का एक quick recall sweep करके ख़त्म करते हैं, revise करने के लिए एक board.
Matter बँटता है pure substances, elements और compounds, और mixtures, homogeneous और heterogeneous में, और change type का एक test है, कोई नया substance बना क्या?
Measurement के लिए, quantity एक number गुणा unit है, one metre cubed है ten to the sixth centimetre cubed, और kelvin है Celsius plus two seven three point one five.
Significant figures के लिए, leading zeros कभी count नहीं होते, trailing zeros सिर्फ़ decimal के साथ, addition decimal places follow करता है, और multiplication significant figures.
पाँच laws हैं conservation, definite, multiple, और reciprocal proportions, और combining volumes, Avogadro के साथ जो volume को moles के proportional देता है।

Mole के लिए, Avogadro's number है six point zero two two times ten to the twenty three, moles बराबर mass over molar mass, number over Avogadro's number, या volume over twenty two point four, और average atomic mass एक weighted mean है।
Formulas के लिए, किसी भी ratio से पहले mass को moles में बदलो, molecular formula है n गुणा empirical formula, और combustion में oxygen difference से निकलता है।

और stoichiometry के लिए, रीढ़ है balance, mole, ratio, back, limiting reagent सबसे छोटा moles over coefficient है, और याद रखो molarity temperature के साथ drift करती है जबकि molality नहीं। यही पूरा chapter है।
